plain_english_title: Effective Dates, 1-Year Lookbacks, Continuous Pursuit & Severance Pay Offset Snapshots
what_this_means: This module provides the exact regulations that determine BOTH the start date of VA disability back pay and whether VA can withhold money from that award: liberalizing law lookbacks (38 C.F.R. § 3.114), general and 1-year increased-rating effective dates (38 C.F.R. § 3.400, especially § 3.400(o)(2)), AMA continuous pursuit across 1-year review steps (38 C.F.R. § 3.2500), Reserve drill-pay and felony-incarceration adjustments (38 C.F.R. §§ 3.654 and 3.665), and recoupment of military disability severance pay or separation pay (38 C.F.R. § 3.700).
record_clues: Medical records showing a service-connected disability clearly worsened within the 12 months BEFORE VA received an increased-rating claim or Intent to File (38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2)), where VA mistakenly used the later C&P exam date instead.
A chain of AMA Supplemental Claims, Higher-Level Reviews, Board appeals, or timely Court appeals filed within 1 year of each prior decision notice (38 C.F.R. § 3.2500(c) and (h)).

A DD-214 or VA Award Letter showing recoupment of Chapter 61 Disability Severance Pay, Separation Pay, or Special Separation Benefits—especially if separation occurred after September 30, 1996 (after-tax cap) or on/after January 28, 2008 for a combat-zone or combat-related injury (zero recoupment allowed).
VA Form 21-8951 (Reserve/National Guard drill-pay waiver) calculating day-for-day training offsets instead of forfeiting an entire year's VA compensation.
important_cautions: Liberalizing law floor (38 C.F.R. § 3.114(a)): when a new statute or VA regulation creates presumptive entitlement (such as the PACT Act), the effective date under § 3.114(a) can never be earlier than the effective date of that new law, and is capped at up to 1 year before the claim if filed more than 1 year after enactment (unless special Nehmer § 3.816 or PACT DIC § 3.33 rules apply).

March 24, 2015 informal-claim shift: since March 24, 2015 (79 FR 57660), VA treatment records alone no longer count as an automatic claim for increase—you must file a complete claim or Intent to File within 1 year of the medically documented worsening to capture the 1-year § 3.400(o)(2) lookback.

Post-court continuous pursuit trap: after an adverse CAVC decision on an AMA appeal, you must file a Supplemental Claim (or Intent to File, per Military-Veterans Advocacy v. Secretary of Veterans Affairs) within 1 year of the CAVC decision if you want to keep your original effective-date chain alive.

Severance pay date cutoffs: VA's complete ban on recouping combat-zone / combat-related Chapter 61 disability severance pay applies strictly to military separations on or after January 28, 2008 (Pub. L. 110-181, § 1646), while the net after-tax recoupment cap applies to separation/severance payments made after September 30, 1996.
questions_for_representative: Did VA mistakenly set my effective date on the date of my C&P examination instead of my Intent to File date, claim date, or up to 1 year earlier under 38 C.F.R. § 3.400(o)(2) for an increased rating?
Have all of my AMA reviews and appeals been filed within 1 year of each decision (or 120 days to the CAVC) to preserve my earliest effective date under 38 C.F.R. § 3.2500?

If VA is withholding separation or disability severance pay from my compensation under 38 C.F.R. § 3.700, did VA cap the recoupment at the net after-tax amount (post-September 30, 1996) or exempt combat-related Chapter 61 severance pay (separated on/after January 28, 2008)?
If I drill in the National Guard or Reserve, did VA properly limit my 38 C.F.R. § 3.654 drill-pay adjustment strictly to the exact number of training days?
